title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Galaxy Rotation Curve Modeling: Comprehensive Analysis of 175 SPARC Galaxies
description: Analyzes 175 galaxies from the SPARC database using an ultra-phenomenological EFC-fit and a simplified ΛCDM-NFW baseline to test the Energy-Flow Cosmology Regime (EFC-R) framework. Finds a strongly significant regime-dependent validity: EFC-fit succeeds in low-complexity FLOW systems (35%) and systematically fails in high-complexity LATENT systems (15%), with reproducible methods and full data/code release.

EFC-fit.description: Ultra-phenomenological rotation-curve turn-on model with asymptotic speed v_flat, radial scale r_turnon, and shape (sharpness) α; used solely for regime mapping.

NFW-circular-velocity.description: Simplified ΛCDM baseline using an NFW halo with fixed concentration c=10, free parameters V200 and r_s.

chi_squared.description: Objective function minimized in fitting; reduced form used for diagnostics.

AIC.description: Model selection criterion with k the number of free parameters.

DeltaAIC.description: Negative values favor EFC-fit; positive values favor ΛCDM-NFW. Thresholds: |ΔAIC| ≥ 10 for strong preference.

latent_proxy.description: Composite proxy of structural complexity using residual–radius Spearman correlation, residual sign-change rate, and normalized reduced χ² (capped).

key_results.main_finding: EFC-fit exhibits regime-dependent validity across SPARC: 100% success in FLOW (62/175, 35.4%) and systematic failure in LATENT (27/175, 15.4%), with highly significant FLOW–LATENT separation (Mann–Whitney U p < 0.0001).
datasets_used: SPARC Database (Lelli et al., 2016), N=175 galaxies, 3,391 points

kill_criteria: KC1: Loss of regime separation — in an independent re-analysis of the full SPARC sample (or larger), the FLOW vs LATENT separation ceases to be statistically significant (Mann–Whitney U p ≥ 0.05) for the published regime metrics.
KC2: Reproducibility failure — running the released code with the documented settings and fixed seed (42) fails to reproduce ≥95% of the published regime labels (FLOW/TRANSITION/LATENT).
KC3: ΛCDM+baryons dominance in FLOW — when a realistic ΛCDM model including baryonic disks/bulges is applied, it strongly outperforms EFC in the FLOW subset (ΔAIC ≥ +10) for ≥80% of FLOW galaxies.

KC4: No systematic failure in LATENT — EFC-fit attains good fits in LATENT systems (χ²_red < 20 and ΔAIC ≤ −10) for ≥70% of LATENT galaxies under robust re-analysis, eliminating the claimed regime-dependent failure.

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper scales the EFC-R regime framework from a pilot N=20 to a comprehensive N=175 SPARC analysis, establishing with high statistical significance (p < 0.0001) that the EFC phenomenological fit exhibits regime-dependent validity: 100% success in FLOW galaxies (62/175) and systematic failure in LATENT galaxies (27/175). It does NOT close any Stage-IV kill criterion or theory gap — it is a T2 empirical foundation paper that builds the evidential base for the regime meta-framework. It introduces its own internal kill criteria (paper-level KC1–KC4) which are distinct from the project-level KC1–KC5.
graph_insights: This paper is currently orphaned in the graph (no 1-hop or 2-hop connections found), which means the SPARC/galactic-scale evidence node is disconnected from the cosmological evidence chain (CMB, BAO, fsigma8). A critical next step is to establish explicit graph connections between the regime framework and the cosmological predictions — e.g., do FLOW-regime galaxies have properties consistent with the EFC cosmological parameter space?

The concepts touched (SPARC, galaxy rotation curves, ΛCDM, NFW, AIC, reduced chi-squared) overlap heavily with MOND literature but no MOND comparison is present in the paper. A graph edge connecting this work to the RAR (Radial Acceleration Relation) literature and McGaugh et al. results would strengthen the contextual positioning and identify whether EFC-R's regime boundaries correlate with the MOND acceleration scale a₀.

The absence of connected validation tests in the graph means this paper establishes a new empirical branch for EFC. It should seed at least 5–7 new test nodes in the validation matrix, covering regime separation, reproducibility, model comparison, and the outstanding paper-level kill criteria.

implicit_consequences: The 100% FLOW success rate and systematic LATENT failure is consistent with EFC's core ontology (E_total = E_flow + E_latent) — FLOW galaxies are dominated by measurable dynamics where the phenomenological model captures physics, while LATENT galaxies harbor unresolved structural complexity (bars, mergers, dense environments) that requires additional physics. This is precisely what a regime framework predicts but has never been demonstrated at this sample size.

The LATENT failure pattern aligns with known ΛCDM small-scale problems (cusp-core, diversity) — the same galaxies that are 'problematic' for standard models are the ones EFC-R explicitly designates as requiring deeper theory. This reframes ΛCDM's galactic anomalies as regime boundary effects rather than model failures.

The paper's internal KC3 (realistic ΛCDM+baryons test in FLOW) is a critical outstanding vulnerability: if ΛCDM with proper baryonic modeling trivially outperforms EFC-fit in FLOW galaxies, the regime claim becomes vacuous. This should be prioritized as a near-term validation action.

The regime classification methodology (complexity metrics → FLOW/TRANSITION/LATENT) can be applied to independent datasets (e.g., THINGS, LITTLE THINGS, upcoming surveys) as a pre-registered prediction pipeline, which would constitute a strong falsifiability demonstration.

No sealed predictions were deposited with this paper — a gap that should be addressed. The regime classification for future surveys (e.g., SKA rotation curves) could be sealed as verifiable forecasts.

This paper is T2 (empirical) and explicitly phenomenological — it deliberately avoids claiming physical theory status, which is strategically correct. The bridge from phenomenological regime mapping to the physical EFC Lagrangian remains an open theory gap.
